News.title: Man, 31, charged with rape and murder after girl, 2, found dead at apartment block
News.content:
TODDLER 'MURDER' Man, 31, charged with rape and murder after girl, 2, found dead at apartment block

A 31-YEAR-OLD man has been charged after a two-year-old girl was found dead at an apartment block.

Cops were scrambled to a property on Pycroft Road in Chertsey, Surrey, on Thursday following reports of concern for safety.





A man has now been charged with murder after the two-year-old girl was found dead inside the home just before 6pm.

Kevin Kerjean, 31, was also charged with rape of a child under 13 and sexual assault of a child under 13.

Surrey Police originally said the girl was aged three, but confirmed on Saturday that she was aged two.

The force, whose major crime team is leading an investigation into the death, said on Thursday they believed it happened “within a family setting”.



Kerjean, a French national who was born in the Central African Republic, appeared at Guildford Magistrates’ Court on Saturday and was remanded ahead of his next appearance at Guildford Crown Court on Monday.

Floral tributes have been left at the entrance to Syward Place, Chertsey, where the girl was found dead.



A message left at the scene read: “RIP beautiful girl. Too good for this earth. May you rest in paradise.”

Local mum Susan Williamson, 31, left flowers at the scene and said: “It’s just so horribly sad.

“I’m a mum and I just wanted to come down here to pay my respects.

The steward of Chertsey Social Club, which is on the opposite side of the road from the flats, Kevin Quirk, said: “I came outside at around 6pm and there were police cars and ambulances everywhere. They had taped off the area.

“It was very unusual to see so many police in one place. They even had an air ambulance land nearby, but I don’t think it was used.



“It’s very unusual to see police cars in this area. It’s so quiet. It’s a really safe community, so when you see that many police cars it does shock you.”

“Everyone is in a state of shock about what has happened. This is a nice area with good people. Things like this don’t usually happen in Chertsey.”

Detective Chief Superintendent Jon Groenen said: “This is a tragic incident, and our thoughts are with the child’s family, as well as all those who knew her.

“Our teams are working hard to build a picture of what happened, and a significant police presence will remain in Pyrcroft Road over the coming days.

“We appreciate that the incident itself, as well as the significant police presence, will be concerning for residents and we would like to thank them for their co-operation as we conduct our investigation.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The force said: “At this stage, we are not looking for anyone else in connection with the incident.”

On Friday, bouquets of flowers were left at the entrance to Syward Place, a flat complex on the corner of Pycroft Road and Bell Bridge Road.

News.title: Four people rushed to hospital after shooting during Cape Verde World Cup celebrations as hundreds partied in Boston
News.content:
FOOTIE HORROR Four people rushed to hospital after shooting during Cape Verde World Cup celebrations as hundreds partied in Boston

AT least four people were rushed to hospital after a shooting, as hundreds partied in Boston after a World Cup game.

Horror struck celebrations after Cape Verde became the smallest country to earn a spot in the World Cup knockout rounds by drawing with Saudi Arabia on Friday night.





Police were called to Brockton, a small town on the outskirts of Boston after reports of a shooting around midnight.

Four people were rushed to hospital with gunshot wounds.

Their current condition is not known.

Cops did not release information about any arrests.

The Massachusetts town of Brockton has the largest Cape Verdean population in the US.

When the tiny island nation’s team made it out of the group stage, hundreds of reportedly flooded the streets to celebrate.

A large group gathered on Main Street, where the shooting was reported.

The Brockton Police Department said in a statement that it had “received multiple reports of gunfire shortly before midnight Friday.”



It comes after at least five people were shot and one person was stabbed after Cape Verde’s previous World Cup match on June 21.

And nine people were injured in a mass shooting just minutes away from England’s World Cup base in Kansas City, Missouri, earlier this month.

Police were called to reports of gunfire on Troost Avenue, a four-mile drive from the training base and team hotel where the Three Lions are staying.

Kansas City Police Department captain Jake Becchina confirmed to The Athletic that three adult females were initially taken to hospital with injuries following the incident.

Police confirmed nine adults had been shot and were all taken to various local hospitals.



All are understood to have suffered non-life threatening injuries.

England’s World Cup base has a tragic gun-ridden past with footie fans already being caught up in highway shootings during the tournament.

Three Lions’ supporters have packed out in Kansas City hoping to be part of English footballing history but multiple violent shootings in the area have sparked questions over their safety in the US.

Four separate shootings were reported to police, including one at Prospect Avenue, around a 15-minute drive from Swope Soccer Village on June, 16 – five days after the World Cup kicked off.

Kansas City police announced a huge manhunt for an alleged killer over a week after one person was shot dead and four others were injured in a shooting spree near England’s base.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Kansas City was also famously the scene of a shooting that left one woman dead and 22 injured at the end of NFL side Kansas City Chiefs’ Super Bowl victory parade in 2024.

News.title: Woman ‘raped’ in city centre park in broad daylight as cops launch hunt for man on bike
News.content:
'RAPE' HORROR Woman ‘raped’ in city centre park in broad daylight as cops launch hunt for man on bike

COPS are investigating reports that a woman was raped by a stranger in a chilling broad daylight attack.

The victim, in her 40s, was allegedly assaulted in Newcastle’s Town Moor park on Tuesday, June 23.



Northumbria Police said she met the attacker on a footbridge leading from Claremont Road into the Spital Tongues area of the city.

The horrific incident took place between 1.15pm and 2.15pm.



Officers say the man fled the scene afterwards on a bike towards Grandstand Road.

Detectives are now hunting the attacker, who is described as a white man in his mid-30s.

The force says he is around 5ft 8in tall, and of muscular build.

He is said to have short dark hair with grey flecks.

Cops say he was wearing black jogging pants and a white t-shirt.

Leading the investigation, Detective Inspector Amanda Dickinson called for help from the public in identifying the suspect.

She said: “I want to recognise the bravery of the victim in coming forward and we are committed to supporting them in any way we can.

“Extensive enquiries have been ongoing and we are now appealing to the public for assistance and asking anyone who was in the area at the time and may have seen anything suspicious to come forward.



“If you do have any information – no matter how insignificant it may seem – please get in touch, as it could prove vital to our investigation.

“While offences of this nature are extremely rare in our area, we recognise the concern they can cause in our communities.

“Since the report we have had an increased presence in the area and would ask anyone who does have any concerns to speak to an officer.

“We are committed to bringing offenders who do commit such offences to justice.”

News.title: Triple murder rocks Rome as ‘killer hacks entire family with meat cleaver’ leaving mum, dad & daughter, 5, dead
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FAMILY MASSACRE Triple murder rocks Rome as ‘killer hacks entire family with meat cleaver’ leaving mum, dad & daughter, 5, dead

A HUGE manhunt has been launched in Rome after a family was allegedly hacked to death by a meat cleaver in a horror triple murder.

Three members of the same family, a mum, dad and their five-year-old daughter were killed in a flat on the western outskirts of the Italian capital.





A fourth member of the family, the 20-year-old son, was hospitalised after the terrifying attack.

Police released a mugshot of Shahadat Hossain, 43, who is wanted on suspicion of murder and assault.

He is thought to have killed the family in a fit of rage after mum Jahan Hosne Momotay rejected his advances.

Hossain, who has a criminal record, had reportedly shown up at the family home in Casalotti to harass Jahan on several previous occasions, but had been sent away.



Investigators think when the woman rejected Hossain for a final time, he killed her and her daughter Arowa with a meat cleaver.

The man then allegedly tried to clean up the blood at the crime scene.

But he was caught in the act by two other members of the family returning home around 10pm, local media claimed.

Dad Arzu Udiu, 38, was killed in the violent confrontation that followed.



His son Amir Hossain Ayon, 20, was also attacked but survived the massacre.

He reportedly told police: “He killed my whole family.

“I got home and saw him cleaning up the blood.



“There was blood everywhere. He killed everyone.”

Amir was rushed to hospital with stab wounds in serious condition.

Neighbours reported hearing piercing screams from the first-floor flat.

They said they then saw a person flee down the street, disappearing into the darkness.

Police seized a meat cleaver, thought to be the murder weapon, from the flat.



Cops are unsure if the alleged murder was pre-planned.

The victims were a Bangladeshi family who had lived in Italy for several years.

Police have launched an investigation and ordered autopsies.

They asked anyone with information about the whereabouts of the suspected killer to come forward.

News.title: Parisians sleep outside as Europe’s heatwave moves west with Germany facing record 42C temperatures & travel chaos
News.content:
PARISIANS have been sleeping outside as Europe continues to experience a sweeping heatwave.

People are turning to city parks to get a good night’s sleep rather than staying inside amid high temperatures with the warm weather moving west towards Germany.





As the heatwave shifts across Europe, temperatures could hit 42C around Berlin as German police deploy water cannons to cool people down.

Cops are patrolling the streets of the capital misting locals and tourists alike.

The country’s transport infrastructure is being severely affected by the heat this weekend, train operator Deutsche Bahn said.

Two sections of a major road outside Berlin have already burst due to soaring temperatures.

Rail companies have advised against all non-essential travel on long-distance and regional trains across the weekend.

In the western city of Dormagen, dozens of residents of a nursing home were evacuated for medical care due to dangerous heat conditions in the building.

The local fire department reported that temperatures inside the home had reached 35C.

A resident at the home died overnight, but it was not yet clear whether the heat was the cause.



France endured its hottest day on record on Wednesday, smashing another record set just the previous day.

Dozens were spotted arriving at Parc des Buttes-Chaumont, in the northeast of Paris, with blankets, hammocks and inflatable mattresses.

Some departments in the west of the country saw highs of over 44C as more than half of the country’s 96 departments were placed on red alert.



The historic heatwave has forced tourist attractions to close and drownings have multiplied as people try to cool off in canals and rivers.

Temperatures have now started to ease as the peak of the heatwave moves on from some regions.

But hospitals remain under intense pressure in the face of severe heat-related emergencies.

The AP-HP authority said its emergency departments treated nearly 3,000 patients on Friday – over a third more than normal.

Temperatures this week have been higher than those during a historic 2003 heatwave that was blamed for 15,000 deaths.



But the AP-HP’s director, Nicolas Revel, said he doesn’t expect as many fatalities this time.



In Italy 18 cities remain on red alert today including popular tourist hotspots Venice, Florence, Bologna and Milan.

Tourists are still trying to cool off in the capital, Rome, seeking shade near buildings and dunking their heads under public fountains.

In the UK conditions are expected to ease across the weekend as the red heat warning drops to amber.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Friday was confirmed as the country’s hottest June day on record, with a provisional temperature of 37C.

It was more than 1C hotter than the long-standing record for June heat set in the summer of 1976.

News.title: The inside story of paranoid loner Derrick Bird who shot dead 12 in 771 minute murder spree before killing himself
News.content:
THE PEACEFUL quiet in rural Cumbria is normally only interrupted by birdsong and the odd tractor rumbling past.

But on one day of horror in 2010 there was also the blast of a shotgun – again and again – as deranged cabbie Derrick Bird launched Britain’s worst massacre since Dunblane.





In 771 minutes of terror he careered around the county taking pot shots at those who he thought had wronged him, close friends and total strangers.

After his shooting spree – which came to an end when he took his own life – 12 people were dead and 11 others had been horrifically injured.

Now, in the latest episode of The Sun’s gripping YouTube series, Inside Stories, we tell how one man turned one of the most picturesque corners of Britain into a killing field.

Bird, 52, lived alone in a tiny terraced house in the village of Rowrah, west Cumbria.



He was well known in the area, drank in local pubs and was a member of a number of clubs including a Sub-Aqua group.

But he was a loner who had struggled to form a new relationship since he split with a long-term partner and he had few close friends.

He holidayed in Thailand with a number of other local men and had met a woman there he considered his girlfriend but they split, triggering mickey-taking from his mates.

That came on the back of regular ribbing by other taxi drivers who thought it was just a laugh, but Bird reckoned it was getting out of hand.



He complained that a tyre had been punctured and milk had been poured into the back seat of his silver Citroën Picasso taxi.

Yet the closest investigators ever got to establishing a motive for his killing spree lay not in his relationship with fellow cabbies, but with his brother and his lawyer.

Bird had developed an obsessive fear that he would be jailed for tax dodging due to thousands in undeclared income.

His twin brother David, 52, and family solicitor Kevin Commons, 60, tried to help him with his financial affairs, but he was so paranoid that he thought they were part of the plot to jail him.

In the early hours of June 2, 2010, dad of two Bird drove the three miles from his home to David’s house in the village of Lamplugh armed with a .22 rifle fitted with a silencer and a sawn-off shotgun.



He gained entry, crept to David’s bedroom and blasted him 11 times.

His body was not found until 11am after he failed to turn up for work.

At 5.14am, Bird arrived at the home of solicitor Kevin Commons, 60. He had known and worked with the Bird family for years and was well liked and trusted by them.

But deranged Bird had become convinced he was also out to get him and lay in wait outside his house for nearly five hours, blocking his drive.

As soon as Kevin got into his car Bird leapt out of his own vehicle and opened fire.



Kevin tried to run back to his house but Bird shot him with his rifle.

As the solicitor was lying critically injured on the ground Bird killed him with a second shot to the head from five yards away.

Having taken care of the two men who were – to his paranoid mind – his main enemies, he drove to the taxi rank in Whitehaven to target those he felt were making his life a misery with their constant mickey-taking and practical jokes.



At 10.27 he pulled up at the back of the town centre rank where the car ahead of him belonged to Darren Rewcastle, 43.

Darren’s mother Betty Scoone later said of her son: “He would do a good turn for anyone. And if he couldn’t do you a good turn he wouldn’t do you a bad one.”

But Bird viewed him as his tormentor-in-chief and when he saw him emerging from a nearby sandwich shop he called him over.

As Darren bent to speak through the open passenger window Bird blasted him in the face with the shotgun. A second shot hit him in the abdomen, killing him instantly.

Bird then shot another taxi driver, Donald Reid, with the rifle, hitting him in the back.



Bird got out of his car and followed Donald as he tried to crawl to safety.

Another stunned cabbie yelled at Bird: “What are you doing?” The gunman turned to get back in his own car and drove off, looping around the one way system to do a drive-by of the rank.

He fired off another couple of shots without hitting anyone before shooting two more cabbies, who survived, as a brave cop flagged down a passing motorist to give chase.

Bird sped off into the countryside, driving through towns and villages where he targeted complete strangers.

In Egremont he spotted secretary Susan Hughes, 57, walking home from shops.



He shot her twice with his shotgun from his driver’s seat, got out, turned her over and shot her a third time with his rifle to make sure she was dead.

He pulled up alongside mole catcher Isaac Dixon, 65, who was checking traps and shot the dad of two twice, killing him.

In a tragic twist he killed a couple in the village of Wilton who were not together but whose paths Bird crossed by chance within a minute of each other.



He first shot account worker Jennifer Jackson, 68, hitting her in the chest with the shotgun and twice in the head with the rifle.

He then drove around the corner and spotted Jennifer’s husband James, 67, chatting to a neighbour.

Bird fired his shotgun from the car, killing the ex-ambulance chief.

Estate agent Jamie Clark, 23, had pulled up by the side of the road to make calls when a colleague contacted him to tell him there had been shooting in the area and to get to safety.

Before he could do anything Bird stopped alongside and blasted him in the head.



In Seascale, a coastal village near the Sellafield nuclear site, Jane Robinson, 66, was delivering Bettaware home catalogues when Bird stopped nearby and called her over to his car.

Tests on her body later showed that the barrel of his shotgun had been touching her mouth when he pulled trigger.

With dozens of armed cops now in pursuit, desperately trying to follow his chaotic and random killing route, Bird sped along a country lane where he crashed into a stone wall near the village of Boot.

He abandoned his taxi and headed into nearby woods where he was found dead a short time later.

Tests show he had knelt down, placed the barrel of his rifle against his forehead and pulled the trigger.



The massacre was over but the devastating effects of it rippled through the years affecting countless people.

To mark the five year anniversary, Darren Rewcastle’s mother Betty did an interview with The Sun and revealed how she still expected him to walk through the door each day.

She said: “They say it gets better over time, I only wish it did.



“I remember it like it was yesterday and it hurts like it was yesterday. Nobody should have to bury their child before them.”

And Terry Kennedy, one of the cabbies who was shot but who survived, incredibly revealed that he bore Bird no resentment.

The pair had been friends for more than 30 years when Bird pulled the trigger and blew away his mate’s right arm.

Terry, who returned to taxiing after getting a prosthetic fitted, said: “He was a bit of a loner but as a bloke he was a decent fella. He just cracked up.

“He’s the last person on earth you’d have thought would do anything like that.”



That summed up the complex question at the heart of the Cumbria shootings – why did Bird do it?

There had been warning signs – a month before he told a scuba diving friend that “Whitehaven will be as famous as Dunblane”, the town in Scotland where 16 school children and their teacher were killed by Thomas Hamilton in 1996.

The friend replied: “Infamous you mean,” and Bird responded: “You will see soon enough.”

And 48 hours before the shooting he said about the taxi drivers who had tormented him: “They are going to get it big style.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The fears he was about to be jailed over his tax affairs appears to have been the final trigger.



But no-one among his friends, family, police or coroner was ever able to exactly pinpoint why he felt the need to take so many innocent victims with him.

News.title: Distraught parents break silence as son-in-law kills himself in jail after arrest for pushing wife off cliff 20yrs ago
News.content:
THE parents of a woman allegedly killed by her husband after she was pushed off a cliff have spoken of their relief following his shock death just days after he was charged with murder.

David Vander Meer, 48, was accused of murder and insurance fraud in connection with the 2006 death of his wife, Bernadette Vander Meer, at Zion National Park, according to the Washington County Attorney’s Office.





Vander Meer, a former church youth pastor, was due to appear at an extradition hearing on Thursday when a Las Vegas judge informed the court that he had died.

A cause of death has not been released but officials cited “self-sustained injuries.”

The charges came after investigators reopened the case following new evidence that challenged the original ruling that it was an accident.

Bernadette, who was 29 and worked at a Las Vegas hotel, died on August 22, 2006, while visiting Utah’s Zion National Park during a trip from the couple’s Las Vegas home.



Prosecutors say Vander Meer pushed his wife from Angels Landing, a steep and narrow trail known for its dramatic cliffs and dangerous drop-offs.

With Vander Meer now dead, the case against him will not proceed to trial.

But in an exclusive interview with The U.S. Sun, Bernadette’s parents, Richard and Laura Gudenkauf, said they were relieved they would not have to revisit their daughter’s death in court after nearly two decades of waiting for answers.

“I am pleased it’s over. I didn’t want to have to go to court, the anxiety that would have caused me,” said Laura.



“His death confirms what we thought happened to Bernadette.”

“She was such a great girl,” added Richard. “It was difficult to have pictures of her around the house. But now, after everything has come out, we have them scattered without the sadness. I didn’t expect that.”

The investigation was reopened in 2022 after a woman came forward with allegations that Vander Meer had groomed her and had a sexual relationship with her when she was a minor in his church youth group.

Investigators said the woman later told them Vander Meer had made a disturbing statement — that they could only be together if his wife was no longer alive.

Prosecutors say Vander Meer killed his wife during an anniversary trip to Zion National Park in August 2006.



He claimed he had stepped away to reposition the couple’s backpacks before taking a photograph when he heard his wife scream.

When he turned around, he said, she was gone.

It was also revealed Vander Meer dramatically increased the couple’s life insurance coverage before the trip, raising each policy from $150,000 to $550,000.

After Bernadette’s death, he collected a $567,439 insurance payout and spent the money on what investigators described as an extravagant lifestyle.

Neither Richard nor Laura said they ever trusted Vander Meer from the beginning of his relationship with their daughter.



“He had an uncomfortable look in his eye,” said Richard. “It was his mannerisms too. It’s hard to put your finger on it, but I told her three weeks after they started dating that I didn’t trust him.



“She was a woman of God and the Bible says you should do what your husband says. That’s what she did. She was the breadwinner.

“She made a ton of money on tips working at the casino. He didn’t really want to work but she still followed him. He was a scoundrel, he knew how to groom young women.”

Laura, who lived with the couple for two years, said she often tried to avoid her son-in-law.

“I just got an uneasy feeling every time I was around him,” she said. “I tried to avoid him most of the time. But she loved him. At the end she was getting fed up, she was going to divorce him.

“I became afraid of him. He was taking advanced weapon training and I didn’t want him picking me off too. Our daughter Vanessa, who is special needs, needs me.”



After Bernadette’s death, a co-worker from the New York-New York Hotel & Casino in Las Vegas contacted police with concerns about the circumstances surrounding the case.

The colleague said she had known Bernadette for six years but had only briefly met her husband once, adding that he rarely attended social gatherings or work events with his wife.

Investigators also looked into Vander Meer’s spending after his wife’s death, including the purchase of a Cadillac SUV worth around $50,000 after the couple sold a condominium.

Within a few years of Bernadette’s passing, Vander Meer was dismissed from his church position amid allegations that he hosted parties for underage church members and provided them with alcohol.

He later married the former church member involved in the allegations. That marriage ended in divorce in 2014.



Despite the nightmare suffered by Laura and Richard over the last 20 years, the Vander Meer family were in their thoughts upon hearing the news about David’s death.

“I will say a prayer for them,” Richard said. “His dad Howard is a great guy and a good friend. They are nice people, they didn’t deserve to be put into this situation by a bad seed.”

Laura said she tried to persuade authorities to reopen the investigation about a year after her daughter’s death but was told the evidence was “circumstantial.”

It sadly took almost two decades to find closure, yet Bernadette’s memory lives on in her beloved parents.

“She was a beautiful woman, a woman of God, sang at church, and affected hundreds of people at different churches,” the mom said. “Everyone loved her. She was wonderful.

“We wanted justice and we wanted him to be stopped. We knew it would come some day. I am just pleased it is over.”

News.title: Met Office issues warning about cold water amid heatwave as Brits dice with death
News.content:
Met Office issues warning about cold water amid heatwave as Brits dice with death

The Met Office has issued a water safety warning after extending its amber heat alerts to Sunday, with parts of the Southeast of England not expected to drop below 20C overnight

View 3 Images Families make a splash in fountains in Reading, Berkshire (Image: Geoffrey Swaine/Shutterstock)

The Met Office has issued a cold water shock warning after extending its amber heat alerts through to Sunday.

‌



Temperatures in parts of the Southeast England are not expected to dip below 20C overnight, prompting the prolonged weather alert. The Met Office has in fact extended an amber weather warning for extreme heat into tomorrow. So, with many Brits flocking to open water to cool off, authorities have reminded families of the dangers at these sites — and not solely linked to swimming.

‌



The Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) told the Met Office cold water also presents a serious health risk because exposure to can lead to "cold water shock," which can become extremely serious. Samantha Hughes, the National Water Safety Partner at the RNLI, said: "It's important to remember that the water is still cold. Entering it unexpectedly can lead to cold water shock, causing a sudden increase in breathing and heart rate, which may trigger panic."

‌



Samantha Hughes, the National Water Safety Partner at the RNLI, said: "It's important to remember that the water is still cold. Entering it unexpectedly can lead to cold water shock, causing a sudden increase in breathing and heart rate, which may trigger panic."

Writing about cold water shock, the Met Office says: "As temperatures rise, many of us are drawn to the water, whether it’s a trip to the beach, a swim in a lake, or a paddle in a river. But while the sun may be shining, the water can still pose serious risks. One of the most dangerous is cold water shock.

"Cold water shock is a sudden and involuntary response that occurs when the body is unexpectedly immersed in water below 15°C. Even on a hot day, the sea, rivers, and lakes in the UK can remain cold enough to trigger this reaction. It’s a physiological response that can affect anyone, regardless of age, fitness, or swimming ability."

‌

This follows the deaths of at least nine people in open water during May's heatwave, the youngest of whom was 12-year-old Junior Slater. The RNLI advises that if you find yourself in difficulty in the water, you should tilt your head back and float.

It added: "If you find yourself struggling in the water, remember to Float to Live: tilt your head back so your ears are submerged, relax and control your breathing. You may need to gently use your hands to help you stay afloat, and it's ok if your legs sink-everyone floats differently.

‌



"Where possible, always choose a lifeguarded beach, and swim between the red and yellow flags. In a coastal emergency remember to call 999 for the coastguard."

The Mirror has, since the deaths last month, led a campaign - Save Lives for Sam - to stop such "catastrophic" tragedies. Some 33 children drown in England every year - "the equivalent of a classroom of children lost". Drowning in the UK has become an "epidemic" and a "national emergency," campaigners say, as we all join forces today to urge the Government to take urgent action.

The Express reports Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service has also urged the public not to jump into open water amid the ongoing heatwave, warning of the dangers of cold water shock.

A spokesperson said: "We urge people to avoid jumping into open water during hot weather. While the air temperature may be high, the water is much colder, and sudden immersion can trigger cold water shock."

The safety campaign was backed by Darren Lloyd, whose son Jack, 16, died after entering Crown Lakes in Farcet.

He said: "It's incredibly difficult to speak out after losing a child, but we've done this to help others and save lives. If you are a young person watching this - you wouldn't want to put your mum and dad through this."

News.title: Andy Burnham's devolution revolution pledge for more local powers to 'rewire Britain'
News.content:
